children.cond: Encephalopathy, hypoglycemia, renal failure or shock — or INR ≥ 1.5 with encephalopathy, ≥ 2.0 without, not corrected by IV vitamin K
Possible acetaminophen ingestion with a raised ALT — including repeated supratherapeutic doses or self-harm

pill.text: Start IV N-acetylcysteine (NAC) now; send acetaminophen level — do not wait for it

children.text: ALT > 15 × ULN with no clear cause: send an acetaminophen level now.

children.cond: Jaundice, pale stools or dark urine · bleeding · ALT > 10 × ULN · liver mass · large liver or spleen, or low platelets

children.subtext: Give IV vitamin K and recheck INR; same-day hepatology
Retest in 24–48 h and refer urgently to hepatology (AASLD 2025)

children.text: Under 11 y: use your lab's age-specific range — the app applies 26/22 from 11 y; AASLD validates it from 10 y.
Write down the ULN you used.
R = (ALT ÷ ALT ULN) ÷ (ALP ÷ ALP ULN). Use the child's own age-specific ALP ULN — growth raises ALP.

pill.text: Cholestasis question: GGT and fractionated bilirubin today

children.tag: Well · ALT < 5 × ULN · no red flags

children.text: Up to 8 weeks if a transient cause is likely (recent viral illness).
No strenuous exercise for ≥ 7 days, ideally 2 weeks, before the repeat.

children.subtext: Stop or review it now — do not wait it out

children.tag: Still raised on repeat · ALT < 5 × ULN

pill.text: Tier 1 workup (First contact); refer if unrevealing

children.text: AST > ALT, or ALT and AST both up in a boy → CK before any other liver test.
Isolated AST with normal ALT and CK → think macro-AST.

children.cond: MASLD suspected, but the child is under 8 y or not overweight

pill.text: Full tier 1 and pediatric hepatology referral — look for other causes first

children.text: Causes: viral (EBV, CMV, HAV, adenovirus) · celiac disease · autoimmune hepatitis (AIH; anti-LKM1: type 2 is typical of young children) · Wilson disease, usually from age 3 · alpha-1 antitrypsin (A1AT) deficiency · drugs · muscle (Duchenne in boys).

children.subtext: Tier 2: 24-h urine copper and slit-lamp exam if ceruloplasmin is low or Wilson is suspected · HBV DNA and HCV RNA if immunosuppressed or high risk, even with negative serology · HIV · IgA, IgM · abdominal Doppler ultrasound

children.text: Tier 3 (specialist): anti-SLA, anti-LC1, AMA, p-ANCA · amino acids, ammonia, blood gas, lactate · carbohydrate-deficient transferrin · lysosomal acid lipase activity · serum bile acids.
3–6-month rule: finish tiers 1–2 within 3–6 months of the first abnormal result. Over 6 months = chronic. Full evaluation within 12 months.

children.subtext: Consider liver biopsy — earlier if AIH or Wilson disease is suspected
